# Detections

The catalog of everything PufferRelay extracts, what it proves, what it cannot prove, and where the output lands. Generated from `detections.yaml`; see `intake.md` before adding an entry.

> Detection is not exploitation. A passive finding says what crossed the wire; verify before acting, and respect the scope.

37 entries: 33 passive, 4 active.

## Inventory (3)

| When | Handler | Detects | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NBNS name/registration frames are present | `netbios` | workstation, domain/browser and service names plus MAC addresses | low | implemented |
| TCP SYN/acknowledgement traffic is present | `services` | observed TCP services per IP (port + resolved service name) | low | implemented |
| IP traffic is present | `ips` | IP inventory grouped by /24 | low | implemented |

### `netbios` — det.netbios

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** the host was advertising these NetBIOS names on the segment  
**Limits:** names are self-asserted; no proof the host still exists  
**Output:** hosts.tsv; leads QW/NETBIOS when anomalous  
**Next:** attach names to IPs and use them for targeting and reporting  
**Capture fields:** nbns.name, nbns.type, arp.src.hw_mac  

### `services` — det.services

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** the service was reachable at capture time  
**Limits:** only observed ports; no banner or version unless another handler sees it  
**Output:** hosts.tsv, nmap-targets.txt  
**Next:** use nmap-targets.txt for verification (ACTIVE, scope-gated)  
**Capture fields:** tcp.flags, tcp.dstport  

### `ips` — det.ips

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** the address was seen on the segment  
**Limits:** a capture from a tap may include unrelated hosts  
**Output:** ips.txt, subnets.txt  
**Next:** scope the engagement around the observed subnets  
**Capture fields:** ip.src, ip.dst  

## Credentials (10)

| When | Handler | Detects | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the capture contains an LDAP bindRequest | `ldap` | the bind identity (usually a DN) and a simple-bind password | critical | implemented |
| HTTP requests are present | `http` | Basic-auth credentials, POST form content, URLs and hosts | critical | implemented |
| FTP control traffic is present | `ftp` | USER/PASS command pairs | critical | implemented |
| Telnet negotiation or data is present | `telnet` | login/password text in the stream (heuristic) | high | implemented |
| SMTP authentication is present | `smtp` | username and password fields | critical | implemented |
| IMAP LOGIN or AUTHENTICATE is present | `imap` | the identity and, for LOGIN, the password parsed from the command line | critical | implemented |
| POP3 USER/PASS or APOP is present | `pop3` | USER/PASS pairs and the APOP identity | critical | implemented |
| SNMP v1/v2c traffic is present | `snmp` | community strings and version | high | implemented |
| HTTP requests/responses carry authentication headers, cookies or token-shaped strings | `httptokens` | Bearer, Vault, GitLab, API-key, session cookies and JWT/GitHub/AWS/Slack/Stripe tokens; decodes JWT claims | critical | implemented |
| Redis, MySQL or PostgreSQL traffic is present | `dbcreds` | Redis AUTH clear text, MySQL login username/response, PostgreSQL startup parameters and clear-text/MD5/SASL auth | critical | partial |

### `ldap` — det.ldap

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** a simple LDAP bind occurred; the password when the simple mechanism was used  
**Limits:** SASL binds expose no password; signing state is not in the packet  
**Output:** credentials.csv; users.txt; leads CRED-*  
**Next:** reuse the bind against LDAP, and check signing separately with relays/coercion  
**Capture fields:** ldap.name, ldap.simple  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/recon/ldap

### `http` — det.http

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** cleartext credentials or form data traversed the wire  
**Limits:** TLS is opaque; NTLM/SSO authentication is handled by the NTLM handler  
**Output:** credentials.csv, hosts.tsv, leads CRED-*  
**Next:** replay Basic auth against the service, then review the form endpoints  
**Capture fields:** http.authorization, http.request.uri, http.file_data  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/web/

### `ftp` — det.ftp

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** cleartext FTP credentials were sent  
**Limits:** FTPS is opaque; binary payloads are not part of the credential row  
**Output:** credentials.csv; leads CRED-*  
**Next:** log in to the FTP service and list shares/data (scope-gated)  
**Capture fields:** ftp.request.command, ftp.request.arg  

### `telnet` — det.telnet

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** cleartext interactive authentication is likely  
**Limits:** heuristic; a prompt without a completed login is not a credential  
**Output:** credentials.csv; leads CRED-*  
**Next:** verify the pair in the surrounding stream before reuse  
**Capture fields:** telnet.data  

### `smtp` — det.smtp

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** mailbox credentials were sent  
**Limits:** TLS submission is opaque; OAuth flows expose no password  
**Output:** credentials.csv; leads CRED-*  
**Next:** test the mailbox credentials; respect lockout policy  
**Capture fields:** smtp.auth.username, smtp.auth.password  

### `imap` — det.imap

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** mailbox credentials were sent  
**Limits:** tshark truncates imap.request.password; AUTHENTICATE may expose only the identity  
**Output:** credentials.csv; leads CRED-*  
**Next:** test the mailbox credentials; check for AUTHENTICATE-only identities  
**Capture fields:** tcp.payload (LOGIN line), imap.request.command  

### `pop3` — det.pop3

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** mailbox credentials were sent  
**Limits:** STLS is opaque; APOP exposes a digest, not the password  
**Output:** credentials.csv; leads CRED-*  
**Next:** test the credentials; APOP digests need offline cracking  
**Capture fields:** pop3.request.command, pop3.request.arg  

### `snmp` — det.snmp

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** a community string was sent in clear text  
**Limits:** SNMPv3 auth/priv is not parsed  
**Output:** credentials.csv; quick win SNMPv1/SNMPv2  
**Next:** query the device with the community (scope-gated); check write access  
**Capture fields:** snmp.community, snmp.version  

### `httptokens` — det.httptokens

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** a reusable secret was sent over HTTP  
**Limits:** TLS is opaque; headers split across TCP segments may be missed; JWT signature is not verified  
**Output:** tokens.tsv (fingerprints); leads TOKEN-*  
**Next:** replay the token (scope-gated); raw values stay in the local database only  
**Capture fields:** http.authorization, http.cookie, tcp.payload, http.file_data  
**Reference:** https://blog.quarkslab.com/a-story-about-confluence-and-tokens.html

### `dbcreds` — det.dbcreds

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** reusable database material or a crackable authentication response was sent  
**Limits:** MSSQL stays with the NTLM handler; SCRAM/native responses need the matching hashcat mode  
**Output:** db-creds.tsv; leads DB-*  
**Next:** reuse clear-text credentials (scope-gated) or crack the response offline  
**Capture fields:** tcp.payload, mysql.user, mysql.passwd, pgsql.parameter_name, pgsql.password, pgsql.authtype  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/infra/protocols/mssql

## Hashes (2)

| When | Handler | Detects | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NTLMSSP messages or HTTP NTLM headers are present | `ntlm` | NetNTLMv1/v2 challenge-response pairs (hashcat 5500/5600) | high | implemented |
| TGS-REQ/TGS-REP exchanges are present | `kerberoast` | TGS-REP service tickets; walks the KDC-REP DER to the ticket enc-part and formats hashcat 13100/19600/19700; reports bursts of five SPNs as candidates | critical | partial |

### `ntlm` — det.ntlm

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** an NTLM authentication exchange was captured and can be cracked offline  
**Limits:** relay feasibility depends on the destination's signing policy (see relays)  
**Output:** ntlm-hashes.txt; leads HASH-*  
**Next:** crack offline; correlate the user with relay-targets.txt  
**Capture fields:** tcp.payload, http.authorization, http.www_authenticate  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/movement/ntlm/

### `kerberoast` — det.kerberoast

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** a service ticket encrypted with the service account hash was issued  
**Limits:** fragmented/unreassembled DER yields a candidate without a hash; SPN-to-account resolution needs directory data  
**Output:** kerberoast-hashes.txt; leads KERBEROAST-*, KERBEROASTCAND-*  
**Next:** crack offline with the matching hashcat mode, then test the service account  
**Capture fields:** kerberos.msg_type, kerberos.SNameString, kerberos.etype, tcp.reassembled.data, udp.payload  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/movement/kerberos/roasting/targeted-kerberoasting

## Kerberos (2)

| When | Handler | Detects | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AS-REQ/AS-REP exchanges are present | `kerberos` | accounts whose AS-REP was returned without pre-authentication (hashcat 18200) | critical | implemented |
| Kerberos AS/TGS exchanges carry delegation or PKINIT padata | `kerberosdepth` | S4U/PA-FOR-USER requests, additional-ticket S4U2Proxy, delegation ticket flags, PKINIT followed by a user-to-user request (UnPAC chain) | high | partial |

### `kerberos` — det.kerberos

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** the KDC returned a crackable AS-REP for that account  
**Limits:** an encrypted AS-REP is not a cracked password; Kerberoasting is separate  
**Output:** asrep-hashes.txt; leads ASREP-*  
**Next:** crack offline, then test the password (scope-gated)  
**Capture fields:** kerberos.msg_type, kerberos.CNameString, kerberos.realm, kerberos.etype, kerberos.padata_type  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/movement/kerberos/roasting/

### `kerberosdepth` — det.kerberosdepth

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** an account can delegate, or a certificate logon was followed by a user-to-user request that enables UnPAC-the-hash  
**Limits:** heuristic from flags/padata; it does not prove the delegation succeeds; hashes are not extracted  
**Output:** kerberos-signals.tsv; leads KERB-*  
**Next:** check the account's delegation rights before using the path  
**Capture fields:** kerberos.padata_type, kerberos.additional_tickets, kerberos.TicketFlags.*  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/movement/kerberos/delegations/

## Ad (7)

| When | Handler | Detects | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NTLM authentication crosses SMB, LDAP or HTTP and the destination signing state is visible | `relays` | relay candidates with source, destination, protocol, user and signing-required flag | high | implemented |
| SMB tree connects, creates or reads are present | `smb` | shares, file names, printer shares and SMB-signing state | medium | implemented |
| Kerberos and ARP frames can be correlated | `asrepcatcher` | relayed AS-REQ from two sources, an AS-REP diverted to a host that did not ask, one IP announced by two MACs, pre-auth-less bursts | critical | partial |
| DCE/RPC binds/requests to EFSRPC, RPRN, DFSNM or FSRVP are present | `coercion` | the coercion interface/pipe and the UNC path from the call data | high | partial |
| HTTP /certsrv enrollment or Kerberos PKINIT is present | `adcs` | certificate enrollment requests (NTLM flagged high) and PKINIT AS-REQ with its principal | high | partial |
| SCCM management/distribution HTTP or SMS shares are present | `sccm` | management point, distribution point, site/package shares and authentication state | high | partial |
| LDAP search results contain sAMAccountName, objectSID or servicePrincipalName | `ldapdir` | SPN-to-account mapping and objectSID when the directory response is captured | medium | partial |

### `relays` — det.relays

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** an NTLM exchange occurred and the destination may accept a relayed authentication  
**Limits:** the capture does not prove a relay was attempted or will succeed  
**Output:** relay-targets.txt, relays.tsv; leads RELAY-*  
**Next:** confirm signing on the destination; use coercion findings for a chain  
**Capture fields:** smb2.sec_mode.sign_required, NTLM fields, protocol ports  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/movement/ntlm/relay

### `smb` — det.smb

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** the client accessed these shares/files; signing was or was not required  
**Limits:** file names come from CREATE/READ frames; content needs smbobjects  
**Output:** smb-shares.txt, smb-files.txt; leads SMB-*, SMBFILE-*  
**Next:** list the shares from the operator host; carve content with smbobjects  
**Capture fields:** smb2.tree, smb2.filename, smb2.sec_mode.sign_required  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/movement/smb/

### `asrepcatcher` — det.asrepcatcher

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** the traffic shape matches ASRepCatcher; ARP spoofing plus a Kerberos signal is critical  
**Limits:** heuristic; a partial capture cannot correlate a reply; not proof of intent  
**Output:** asrepcatcher.txt; leads ASREPCATCHER-*; console panel with the repo link  
**Next:** review the evidence; the lead links https://github.com/Yaxxine7/ASRepCatcher  
**Capture fields:** kerberos.msg_type, kerberos.CNameString, kerberos.padata_type, arp.opcode, arp.src.proto_ipv4, arp.src.hw_mac  
**Reference:** https://github.com/Yaxxine7/ASRepCatcher

### `coercion` — det.coercion

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** a victim was told to authenticate to a host (the first half of a relay chain)  
**Limits:** encrypted RPC is opaque; a bind or pipe without a UNC path is normal traffic and is ignored  
**Output:** coercions.tsv; leads COERCE-*  
**Next:** look for the matching NTLM exchange to the UNC host and review relay-targets.txt  
**Capture fields:** dcerpc.cn_bind_to_uuid, dcerpc.opnum, smb2.filename, tcp.reassembled.data  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/movement/mitm-and-coerced-authentications/rpc-coercions/

### `adcs` — det.adcs

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** certificate enrollment or certificate logon was observed  
**Limits:** template attributes are usually not visible; DCOM-only enrollment is not fully parsed  
**Output:** adcs.tsv; leads ADCS-*  
**Next:** review the CA/template and whether the enrolling host should be able to do this  
**Capture fields:** http.request.uri, http.authorization, kerberos.padata_type  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/movement/adcs/

### `sccm` — det.sccm

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** SCCM management traffic was observed; NTLM to a management point is a relay candidate  
**Limits:** SMS Provider DCOM and policy objects are not parsed; package delivery alone is inventory  
**Output:** sccm.tsv; leads SCCM-*  
**Next:** review the endpoint and authentication; correlate with relay findings  
**Capture fields:** http.request.uri, http.host, http.authorization, smb2.tree  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/movement/sccm-mecm/

### `ldapdir` — det.ldapdir

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** the service principal belongs to that account in the observed directory data  
**Limits:** attribute/value pairing is positional and can be confused by commas or split entries  
**Output:** ldap-spns.tsv; leads SPN-*; objectSID upgrades BloodHound identifiers  
**Next:** join the SPN with the Kerberoast hash/lead for the same service  
**Capture fields:** ldap.AttributeDescription, ldap.AttributeValue  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/recon/ldap

## Network (5)

| When | Handler | Detects | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EAPOL/EAP or RADIUS frames are present | `nac` | 802.1X/MAB identities, authenticator and method | low | implemented |
| HTTP requests look like Windows Update/WSUS | `wsus` | WSUS endpoints, hosts and indicators | medium | implemented |
| DNS queries/answers are present | `dns` | query name, record type, A/AAAA/PTR answer; attaches names to host IPs | low | implemented |
| DHCPv6, ICMPv6 router advertisements or DNS UPDATE are present | `ipv6` | offered DNS servers, RDNSS/DNSSL, and ADIDNS dynamic updates; one host doing both is critical | critical | implemented |
| SIP or Cisco Skinny/SCCP signalling is present | `voip` | SIP methods (REGISTER/INVITE/MESSAGE), caller/callee, Call-ID, digest auth presence; Skinny call party metadata | medium | implemented |

### `nac` — det.nac

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** port authentication is in use and which identities authenticate  
**Limits:** no keys; spoof proposals are Tier B and not generated here  
**Output:** nac.txt; leads NAC-*  
**Next:** decide whether the port is defended before any active test  
**Capture fields:** eapol, eap, radius User-Name  

### `wsus` — det.wsus

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** the client contacted update infrastructure  
**Limits:** approval state and package integrity are not visible  
**Output:** wsus.txt; leads WSUS-*  
**Next:** check whether the WSUS server itself is trustworthy and patched  
**Capture fields:** http.host, http.request.uri, http.user_agent  

### `dns` — det.dns

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** the name was resolved to that address during the capture  
**Limits:** one answer per row when a response carries several records; DoH/DoT is opaque  
**Output:** dns.txt; hostnames in hosts.tsv  
**Next:** use the name map for targeting and reporting; check ADIDNS separately  
**Capture fields:** dns.qry.name, dns.qry.type, dns.flags.response, dns.a, dns.aaaa  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/recon/dns

### `ipv6` — det.ipv6

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** a host is offering DNS via IPv6 and/or updating AD-integrated DNS  
**Limits:** no baseline of the legitimate resolver; confirm before calling it rogue  
**Output:** ipv6.tsv; leads IPV6-*  
**Next:** identify the offering host and compare it with the known resolver  
**Capture fields:** dhcpv6.msgtype, dhcpv6.dns_server, icmpv6.type, icmpv6.opt.rdnss, dns.flags.opcode  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/movement/mitm-and-coerced-authentications/dhcpv6-spoofing

### `voip` — det.voip

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** call signalling was visible in clear text and which endpoints registered/called  
**Limits:** media (RTP) is not decoded; TLS/SIPS is opaque; digest challenges are not cracked  
**Output:** voip.tsv; leads VOIP-*  
**Next:** review the registrar/PBX exposure and the extension map  
**Capture fields:** sip.Method, sip.from.user, sip.to.user, sip.Call-ID, sip.Authorization, skinny.CallingPartyNumber  

## Files (2)

| When | Handler | Detects | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HTTP responses or FTP-DATA carry file objects | `files` | object name, type, size and sha256; writes the bytes to files/ | medium | implemented |
| SMB traffic carries file objects that tshark can reassemble | `smbobjects` | file content, name, type and sha256 exported through the captured-files pipeline | medium | implemented |

### `files` — det.files

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** the object crossed the wire and can be inspected locally  
**Limits:** 1 MiB/object, 16 MiB/capture; TLS and segmented SMB are opaque  
**Output:** files.tsv, files/; leads FILE-*  
**Next:** inspect interesting objects locally; never upload them  
**Capture fields:** http.file_data, ftp.data, http.content_type  
**Reference:** https://github.com/vikwin/pcapfex

### `smbobjects` — det.smbobjects

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** the object crossed SMB and can be inspected locally  
**Limits:** 8 MiB/object, 16 MiB/capture; SMB3 encryption and missing reassembly yield nothing  
**Output:** files.tsv, files/  
**Next:** inspect interesting objects locally; keep the output on the engagement machine  
**Capture fields:** tshark --export-objects smb  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/movement/smb/

## Weakness (1)

| When | Handler | Detects | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| -q is used, or -f is combined with -q | `quickwins` | SMBv1, missing SMB/LDAP signing, SNMPv1/v2, SSLv2/v3, TLS1.0, LLMNR/NBT-NS/mDNS, cleartext protocols | varies | implemented |

### `quickwins` — det.quickwins

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** a weak protocol or configuration was observed on the wire  
**Limits:** presence is not exploitability; signing may be enforced elsewhere  
**Output:** quick_wins table; leads QW-*  
**Next:** confirm the weak setting from the operator host (ACTIVE, scope-gated)  
**Capture fields:** one tshark pass over the quick-win fields  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/movement/mitm-and-coerced-authentications/llmnr-nbtns-mdns-spoofing

## Ai (1)

| When | Handler | Detects | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HTTP traffic targets an LLM service, MCP endpoint or vector database | `llm` | service, endpoint, model, auth-header presence, MCP method and tool names | critical | partial |

### `llm` — det.llm

**Mode:** passive  
**Proves:** which AI service is in use and whether it was reached without authentication  
**Limits:** TLS is opaque; ambiguous ports are recognised only by path markers; prompts are not exported  
**Output:** llm.tsv; leads LLM-*  
**Next:** review exposure; an unauthenticated inference endpoint is the critical case  
**Capture fields:** http.host, http.request.uri, tcp.dstport, tcp.payload, http.file_data  
**Reference:** https://blog.quarkslab.com/agentic-ai-the-confused-deputy-problem.html

## Active (4)

| When | Handler | Detects | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no capture exists yet and you can capture on an authorized interface | `live` | whatever the mandatory BPF filter matches, analysed like a pcap | varies | implemented |
| you need to observe one TCP target through a local relay | `proxy` | both directions of the relayed stream, recorded as JSONL (base64 chunks) | varies | implemented |
| the inventory suggests an ARP/relay path and you want reviewable commands | `commands` | nothing; it generates text (ARP spoof, ettercap, relay) for relay-relevant hosts | varies | implemented |
| you want a next-step command per host or finding | `serveme` | nothing; it generates text from the passive inventory | varies | implemented |

### `live` — active.live

**Mode:** active  
**Proves:** nothing by itself; the same passive handlers do the work  
**Limits:** requires --live, --bpf and --duration; red warning and authorization; temp file deleted unless kept  
**Output:** same as -f; --keep-live-capture keeps the temporary pcap  
**Next:** confirm written scope before running; start with a narrow filter  

### `proxy` — active.proxy

**Mode:** active  
**Proves:** the bytes that crossed the relay; not a pcap  
**Limits:** one target, bounded duration, explicit warning and authorization  
**Output:** proxy-recording.jsonl  
**Next:** confirm scope; prefer a passive capture when one is available  

### `commands` — active.commands

**Mode:** active  
**Proves:** the commands are suggestions, not executed actions  
**Limits:** text only; every line is ACTIVE and includes cleanup  
**Output:** active-commands.md  
**Next:** review scope and cleanup before running anything  
**Reference:** https://www.thehacker.recipes/ad/movement/mitm-and-coerced-authentications/arp-poisoning

### `serveme` — active.serveme

**Mode:** active  
**Proves:** suggestions derived from the capture  
**Limits:** text only; ACTIVE lines are marked  
**Output:** serveme.md  
**Next:** review each command and its scope warning
